record.original_question: Is there a birack whose induced action on virtual braids is faithful, and is the known invariant of virtual braids cited in [87] and [74, 3, 51] faithful?

evidence.quote: Is there a birack such that its action on virtual braids is faithful? Is the invariant of virtual braids in [87], see also [74, 3, 51] faithful?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A birack is a set $X$ equipped with a bijection $S: X\times X \to X\times X$ satisfying the set-theoretic Yang–Baxter equation $(S\times \mathrm{id})(\mathrm{id}\times S)(S\times \mathrm{id}) = (\mathrm{id}\times S)(S\times \mathrm{id})(\mathrm{id}\times S)$, together with the usual birack invertibility/sideways-reversibility axioms ensuring that $S$ encodes a coloring rule preserved under Reidemeister moves. Any birack $(X,S)$ induces an action of the virtual braid group $VB_n$ on $X^n$: the classical generator $\sigma_i$ acts by $S$ on the $i,i+1$ factors, while the virtual generator $\tau_i$ acts by the transposition on those factors. This yields a homomorphism $\rho_{X,S}: VB_n \to \mathrm{Sym}(X^n)$ (or, more generally, into the symmetric group of colorings), and hence an associated invariant of virtual braids.

Question 1. Does there exist a birack $(X,S)$ (with $X$ possibly infinite) such that the induced homomorphism $\rho_{X,S}: VB_n \to \mathrm{Sym}(X^n)$ is faithful for every $n\geq 2$?

Question 2. Is the standard combinatorial/diagrammatic invariant of virtual braids obtained from the universal birack-type coloring construction a faithful invariant of virtual braids — i.e., does it distinguish every pair of inequivalent virtual braids?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search reveals active research on birack-based invariants of virtual braids and links, with enhancements (birack modules, switch braid quivers, Dynnikov-type coordinates) yielding stronger invariants. However, no source clearly establishes the existence of a birack whose induced action on virtual braids is faithful, nor a proof or disproof that the standard combinatorial invariant of virtual braids is faithful. The status appears to remain open or unresolved in the publicly available literature.

status_evidence.title: Birack modules and their link invariants
status_evidence.snippet: Birack module enhanced invariants are strictly stronger than the unenhanced birack counting invariant, and are not determined by the Jones or Alexander polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Birack invariants continue to be enhanced; no faithfulness result for virtual braids is reported.

status_evidence.title: Biracks and Switch Braid Quivers
status_evidence.snippet: Switch structures on permutation representations of the braid group and quiver-valued invariants of braids.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work refines birack invariants of braids but does not claim a faithful birack action on virtual braids.

status_evidence.title: Dynnikov coordinates on virtual braid groups
status_evidence.snippet: Linear/coordinate representations for virtual braid groups.
status_evidence.claim: Various representations of virtual braid groups exist; faithfulness of birack-induced actions in general is not established.
